claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children, and could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I'm responsible for one child. His name is Alex and he's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 16 years old, there are some additional factors I need to check.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he still in school, college, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school anymore, but he has started an apprenticeship in Belfast.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail:

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it specifically an apprenticeship program in Northern Ireland/Belfast?**

This distinction is important because the rules specifically mention apprenticeships in England.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's specifically in Northern Ireland - he's doing his apprenticeship in Belfast.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. **How many hours per week is Alex working in his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact hours, but it's full-time - he's there during normal working hours throughout the week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions:

1. **Do you live in the UK?**

2. **Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. And no, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me carefully consider Alex's situation based on the Child Benefit rules.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 16 years old
- He's no longer in approved education or training
- He's doing a full-time apprenticeship in Northern Ireland (Belfast)
- He's working full-time hours (which would typically be 24+ hours per week)
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- You live in the UK

The key rule here is that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child "starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training" OR "starts an apprenticeship in England."

Since Alex is working full-time (which typically means 24+ hours per week) and is no longer in approved education or training, this would make you ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex, even though his apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland rather than England.

The rules state that Child Benefit stops when a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.

If you're currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, you should contact HMRC to inform them of this change in circumstances.
